settings.title: Settings
settings.serverInfo:
Choose where your encrypted files are stored.

StealthCloud uses our secure zero-knowledge cloud server.
Local connects to your own server on the same WiFi network.
Remote connects to your own server hosted anywhere — VPS, dedicated server, or any machine with a public IP.
settings.localServerInfo:
Connect to a PhotoLynk server running on your local network.

Enter the IP address and port of the computer running the server.
settings.remoteServerInfo:
Connect to your own PhotoLynk server hosted remotely — such as a VPS, dedicated server, or any machine with a public IP.

You run the server yourself and control your data. Enter the domain or IP address where your server is hosted.
settings.preferencesInfo:
Customize app behavior.

Auto Upload backs up new photos automatically when your device is on WiFi and charging.

Fast Mode increases upload speed but uses more battery.
settings.autoUploadOnDesc: New photos will be backed up automatically
settings.autoUploadNote: Background uploads depend on iOS/Android policies. For best results: keep the app open occasionally, connect to WiFi, and charge your device.
settings.englishDefaultNote: English is the default if your system language is not supported.
settings.dangerZoneInfo:
These actions permanently delete data. Use with caution.

Deleting server data removes all your encrypted backups.
This cannot be undone.
settings.deleteAccountWarning: This will permanently delete your account and all data. This action cannot be undone.
settings.fullEncryptionDesc: When enabled, files are encrypted before upload. Server cannot read your data. When disabled, files upload 2-5x faster but without encryption.
settings.encryptionRecoveryDesc: Your wallet generates the encryption key. Same wallet = automatic recovery. This key is a backup for PC recovery without a Solana phone.
settings.encryptionRecoveryInfo:
Your photos are encrypted with a master key before upload.

KEYS: Tap 'Reveal Encryption Key(s)' to see your master key(s). Save them as a last-resort backup — if you lose your phone and don't have the recovery kit, you can provide these keys to support for manual file recovery.

RECOVERY KIT: Tap 'Create Recovery Kit' to generate an encrypted backup of your credentials protected by a PIN. On any Android phone, paste the kit and enter your PIN to restore your account automatically — no support ticket needed.
settings.encryptionKeyUnavailable: Encryption key not available. Please log out and log in again.
settings.keySecureInfo: Save this as a backup. Same wallet on any phone regenerates it automatically.
settings.keyLegacyInfo: For older files. Works automatically — no action needed.
settings.encryptionUpgradeDesc: Runs while the app is open. Pauses when you switch away and resumes on return. No uploads needed.
settings.encryptionUpgradeInfo:
This upgrades your file manifest encryption to a stronger wallet-signature-derived key.

It only re-encrypts the small manifest wrapper on the server — no photos are re-uploaded.

The app must stay open to process. It pauses if you switch apps and resumes when you return.

It does not interfere with backups or sync.
settings.encryptionEnhancedDesc: All files upgraded. Same wallet = easy recovery on any device.
settings.encryptionSecureDesc: Your files are encrypted with a wallet-signature-derived key. Same wallet on any device regenerates the key automatically.

nftWelcome.title: Certifying Your Photos
nftWelcome.subtitle: Create a tamper-proof authenticity record for any photo. Your photo stays safe — only a verified proof goes on record. Pick the option that fits your goal.
nftWelcome.publicName: Share, sell, or use as avatar
nftWelcome.publicDesc: Open Edition + Decentralized Storage + Unencrypted. Your photo is uploaded to permanent decentralized storage. Metadata is recorded for verification. Anyone can view the image. Ideal for portfolios, social profiles, or selling prints.
nftWelcome.publicPro1: Viewable in any compatible viewer or browser
nftWelcome.publicPro2: Photo quality — no compression, no re-encoding
nftWelcome.publicPro3: Optional watermark to protect your work
nftWelcome.publicCon2: EXIF (location, camera) visible unless you strip it
nftWelcome.privateName: Encrypted backup — only you can view
nftWelcome.privateDesc: Open Edition + Decentralized Storage + Encrypted. Same as above, but the image is encrypted on your device before upload. The file in storage is unreadable without your key. Ownership recorded, image stays private.
nftWelcome.privatePro2: Decryption key sealed to your credentials — your private key never leaves the device
nftWelcome.privatePro4: Stored on decentralized storage — no company can delete it
nftWelcome.privateCon1: Others see an encrypted blob, not the image
nftWelcome.privateCon2: Cannot be used as a public avatar or shared as-is
nftWelcome.certDesc: Limited Edition + Embedded + Encrypted. Your photo and metadata are stored directly inside the authenticity record.
nftWelcome.certPro1: No external dependencies — image is stored inside the record, not on a separate server
nftWelcome.certPro2: RFC 3161 timestamp from FreeTSA.org — accepted in legal proceedings
nftWelcome.certPro3: C2PA manifest — industry standard used by Adobe, Microsoft, BBC
nftWelcome.certPro4: Certificate of Authenticity — proves you took the photo, when, and with what camera
nftWelcome.certPro5: Permanent record — no cloud subscription, no link rot
nftWelcome.certCon1: Larger metadata — costs more than a simple upload
nftWelcome.certCon2: Not viewable as a regular image in viewers (encrypted data)
nftWelcome.factImageDesc: Your photo is never compressed or re-encoded. The record type refers to how the verification record is stored — your image stays pixel-perfect. All records have identical authenticity regardless of storage method.
nftWelcome.factExifDesc: Date, GPS, camera model, and serial number are preserved by default. You can strip EXIF before certifying for privacy. Limited Edition always hashes EXIF for proof without exposing it.
nftWelcome.factEncryptionDesc: Done on your device with AES-256-GCM before anything is uploaded. The decryption key is sealed to your credentials via a signature request — your private key never leaves the device. No server ever sees the photo.
nftWelcome.factPublicDesc: Only unencrypted storage options make your image public. Everything else — encrypted storage, encrypted embedded, or Limited Edition — keeps your image private.
